implement.name: Purity
implement.summary: A function whose result depends only on its arguments and whose evaluation changes nothing outside its return value; the impure boundary is named where it is

implement.name: Total functions
implement.summary: Every input maps to an output; failure is a value the signature carries, not a throw the runtime raises

implement.name: Referential transparency
implement.summary: An expression is replaceable by its value without changing the program's behaviour, and any expression that fails this is the leak to find

implement.name: Immutability by default
implement.summary: A value that mutates when an equivalent immutable value would have written less, and the line where mutation becomes acceptable

implement.name: Composition over inheritance
implement.summary: Inheritance is not the default reuse mechanism; typeclasses, extension functions and function composition are the smaller, more local choice when it fits

implement.name: Effect discipline
implement.summary: An effect is described as a value the program composes, executed at the boundary — not performed at the call site

review.name: A misplaced rule is a finding
review.summary: A rule that can only be stated in one language's terms belongs to that language's module; the review names it and proposes the move before the PR merges

review.name: Functional Programming paradigm review
review.summary: Measure a change against the six principles, finding by finding, each citing the rule it broke

find-spec.name: Paradigm rules reach the spec
find-spec.summary: The same six principles apply when loading the spec context a ticket needs; finding the rule and the spec is one operation, not two
